headline: Ground Broken for Metro Manila Subway's NAIA Terminal 3 Station
seoTitle: Metro Manila Subway NAIA Terminal 3 Station Breaks Ground | FMB News
seoDescription: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. led the September 16 groundbreaking for the Metro Manila Subway's NAIA Terminal 3 Station, according to government and independent reports.
deck: The groundbreaking marks a new construction milestone for the planned subway connection at Ninoy Aquino International Airport Terminal 3. It does not mean the station is already operational.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. led the groundbreaking ceremony Wednesday for the Metro Manila Subway Project's planned NAIA Terminal 3 Station at Ninoy Aquino International Airport.
The event was reported by the Philippine News Agency and independently covered by ABS-CBN News and GMA News. The ceremony is a construction milestone; the station is not yet open to passengers.

sections.heading: What is confirmed
paragraphs: Government coverage identifies the project as the NAIA Terminal 3 Station of the Metro Manila Subway. ABS-CBN News published independent coverage of the groundbreaking at 4:55 p.m. PHT on September 16, while GMA carried the ceremony live.
FMB News is limiting this update to the confirmed groundbreaking and is not treating projected completion or travel-time claims as accomplished outcomes.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The Metro Manila Subway is a major rail project designed to create an underground north-south mass-transit corridor across Metro Manila. The airport station is intended to integrate NAIA Terminal 3 into that network once construction, systems work, testing and commissioning are completed.

Large infrastructure projects can experience schedule, right-of-way, procurement and construction changes. Any future opening date should therefore be treated as a project target until formally achieved.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: A functioning airport rail connection could give passengers and airport workers another public-transport option and connect NAIA Terminal 3 to the wider subway network. Wednesday's groundbreaking advances that objective from planning toward physical construction at the airport station site.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for Department of Transportation construction updates, civil-works progress at the airport station, integration with other subway contract packages and formal revisions to the project's completion timetable. FMB News will report material construction milestones separately when verified.

verificationNotes: Philippine News Agency's September 16 headline service identifies President Marcos as breaking ground for the NAIA Terminal 3 station.
ABS-CBN News independently reported the groundbreaking at 4:55 p.m. PHT.
GMA News carried the September 16 ceremony as a live event and replay.
The article distinguishes the groundbreaking from completion or operation and does not present projected benefits as already realized.

The contextual hero depicts actual Metro Manila Subway construction at Quezon Avenue Station, not the NAIA event. Wikimedia Commons identifies uploader Valenzuela400 as the copyright holder and licenses the photograph under CC BY-SA 4.0; the caption makes the archival context explicit.
